rawRetro.summary: Fixed the CRM server files that failed verification: corrected the authorization type imports, removed a dead filter helper, and repaired several TypeScript errors in server/crm/service.ts and server/crm/domain.ts. Lint, Prettier and all three TypeScript projects now pass for the affected scope. | Repaired the failures that blocked verification and finished the CRM feature. Fixed the seed module specifiers, registered the crm composite resource through a new service provider, repaired the shadcn cn imports, made the CRM client lint-clean under react-hooks/set-state-in-effect, and fixed the READ_FORBIDDEN write policy on follow-ups. Then implemented the remaining HTTP surface and client pages. Server/client/npm lint, typecheck, all 245 tests, the production build, a fresh-database db apply, a live HTTP smoke test and a scripted browser flow all pass. | Verification-repair round: fixed the opportunity Amount column rendering '—' (decimal columns are decoded as strings; normalised to numbers at the CRM service view boundary) and made the customers list refetch when returning from the import child route (useLoad key now includes location.key). Verified with a new server integration test and a new client navigation test, plus lint/prettier/typecheck on the affected files.

issues.title: Unsafe-any ESLint errors in server/crm/access.ts
issues.symptom: eslint reported 13 errors in server/crm/access.ts: @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment, no-unsafe-member-access on .conditions/.effect, and no-unnecessary-type-assertion. AuthorizationDecision resolved to an error type, so every member access on a decision was 'on a type that cannot be resolved'.
issues.rootCause: access.ts imported AuthorizationDecision and AuthorizationContext from '@nocobase/app-plugin-authorization', whose server entry only re-exports AuthorizationContext (and Authorization, etc.) as types. AuthorizationDecision was not exported there, so TypeScript fell back to an error type; CompositeResourceConditions was imported from '@nocobase/authorization/core' separately.
issues.resolution: Import AuthorizationContext from '@nocobase/app-plugin-authorization' and both AuthorizationDecision and CompositeResourceConditions from '@nocobase/authorization/core', where they are actually declared. No behavior change.

issues.title: Unsafe-any ESLint errors in server/crm/service.ts
issues.symptom: eslint reported at service.ts:650 unsafe return/call/member-access on '.number(...).eq(...)', 5 errors.
issues.rootCause: listContacts contained a leftover dead helper `const filter = (builder) => builder.number('customerId').eq(query.customerId ?? -1); void filter;` whose untyped parameter made the builder `any`.
issues.resolution: Deleted the dead helper; the real filter is built inline inside findMany/count.

issues.title: TypeScript errors surfaced by tsconfig.server.json after the lint fixes
issues.symptom: tsc -p tsconfig.server.json reported: (367) 'id' not assignable to RepositoryFilter<T>; (676) array with undefined not assignable to readonly FilterNode[]; (690) unnecessary/incorrect FilterNode type predicate; (1236) SuggestionRow not assignable to SuggestionDraft because SuggestionRow.kind is string while SuggestionDraft.kind is the SuggestionKind union.
issues.rootCause: The generic visibleChild<T extends object> could not infer T's fields for the shorthand filter { id }, and its RepositoryFilter type rejected the object; the listContacts count filter array mixed optional entries and relied on a type predicate; suggestionKey was over-typed to SuggestionDraft although it only reads four fields.
issues.resolution: Constrained visibleChild to T extends { id: number } and expressed its filter through builder.number('id').eq(id); extracted a shared typed filterContacts builder used by findMany and count; widened suggestionKey's parameter to a structural { kind: string; customerId; opportunityId; followUpId } type. All three tsc projects (root, tsconfig.node.json, tsconfig.server.json) now pass.

issues.title: Seeds could not be loaded: unresolvable module specifiers
issues.symptom: All 28 tests in tests/logic/app-server.test.ts failed with AppDatabaseTaskError while running database/main seeds: the permission-set seed imported "../../seed-data/permission-sets.js" and that seed-data module imported "../../server/crm/resources.js". Native Node type-stripping (Node 24) loaded the .ts seed sources and could resolve neither the .js nor an extensionless specifier.
issues.rootCause: Node native ESM does not apply the TypeScript .js-to-.ts rewrite that tsc-alias applies at build time, so a .js specifier written for the compiled output does not resolve against the TypeScript source when the seed is executed directly by the loader (vitest externalizes @nocobase/db, so the raw .ts is what runs).
issues.resolution: Changed the two relative specifiers to point at the actual .ts files (../../seed-data/permission-sets.ts and ../../server/crm/resources.ts). tsc/tsc-alias still rewrite them to .js for the compiled build.

issues.title: Authorization startup rejected the seeded crm permission sets
issues.symptom: After the import fix, application startup threw "Authorization has invalid stored grants: Permission set crm-sales grants composite:crm.view, which no longer applies: Unknown composite resource action: crm.view" (and crm.edit/crm.delete, crm.suggest/crm.manageTeam for crm-sales-manager), from @nocobase/app-plugin-authorization/server/stored-grants.ts via AuthorizationProvider.start.
issues.rootCause: A composite resource must be registered before stored grants that reference it can be validated, but nothing registered the crm composite declared in server/crm/resources.ts. server/providers/index.ts was empty, so the resource was never defined in the runtime authorization registry.
issues.resolution: Added server/crm/tokens.ts (crmServiceToken) and server/providers/crm.ts (CrmProvider): it binds the CRM service, registers the five CRM collections with the authorization database, calls authz.compositeResources.define(crm), and places the composite under a crm subsection of the built-in business section. Registered CrmProvider in server/providers/index.ts. Collections are registered before the composite is defined because grant validation resolves write fields against registered collections.

issues.title: CLI-generated UI primitives imported cn from a bare "cn" specifier
issues.symptom: Client compilation failed for client/components/ui/{checkbox,table,select,card,badge}.tsx: Cannot find module "cn".
issues.rootCause: The shadcn CLI emitted some primitives with an import of "cn" instead of the application alias "@/lib/utils".
issues.resolution: Corrected the import specifier in the five generated files to "@/lib/utils". These files are otherwise left exactly as the CLI wrote them.

issues.title: react-hooks/set-state-in-effect errors across the CRM client
issues.symptom: eslint --max-warnings 0 failed with react-hooks/set-state-in-effect (and the @eslint-react equivalent) on the data-loading hook, the option hooks, and the four form dialogs, which all wrote state synchronously inside useEffect.
issues.rootCause: The obvious patterns (setState at the top of an effect to mark loading, and reset effects that re-seed form state when a record changes) are exactly what the strict rule forbids.
issues.resolution: Rewrote client/pages/crm/use-load.ts so the effect only starts a request and writes state from the promise callbacks, deriving loading from whether the cached snapshot key matches the requested key. Dropped the reset effects from the four form dialogs (state is now initialised lazily from the record) and made the list/detail pages mount each dialog conditionally with a per-open key, so it re-initialises on every open. Moved followUpIsOverdue out of components.tsx into format.ts so that file only exports components (react-refresh/only-export-components).

issues.title: Approving an assistant suggestion returned 403 READ_FORBIDDEN
issues.symptom: POST /api/crm/suggestions/:id/decide with {decision:"approve"} answered 403 with reason READ_FORBIDDEN ("Reading from this Repository is forbidden by Policy.", domain app). The create itself happened first, but the repository refused the read-back. Dismiss worked. Creating contacts, opportunities and follow-ups through their own endpoints was also affected because they share the write policy.
issues.rootCause: The followUpWrite database permission in server/crm/resources.ts declared .create("*").update("*") but no .read("*"). The authorization plugin folds a composite action's grants into a RepositoryPolicy in which an undeclared operation is false, and Repository.createOne/updateOne perform an internal read context before writing. Binding the edit policy therefore made every write through it fail on the read node. The other write permissions (customers, contacts, opportunities) already declared .read("*"), which is why only follow-ups failed.
issues.resolution: Added .read("*") to followUpWrite so the edit action covers the read-back, consistent with the other write permissions. Verified against the live application: suggestion approval, followUp create/update/delete, and contact/opportunity create all succeed, and the whole repository flow was re-tested in a real browser.

issues.title: CRM feature had no HTTP surface and no client pages
issues.symptom: The previous round left the CRM domain layer (server/crm/*) in place but server/routes/index.ts contributed no routes and client/routes.ts declared no CRM pages, so the browser acceptance could not exercise the feature at all.
issues.rootCause: The feature was only partly built; the route layer and the whole client were missing.
issues.resolution: Implemented the full HTTP surface in server/routes/crm.ts with server/routes/schemas.ts (zod validation via apiValidator, describeRoute declarations, permission-before-validation through a crmAction middleware, ApiError mapping for denied/not-found) and the client under client/pages/crm/ (dashboard, customers list/detail/import, opportunities, follow-ups, form dialogs, suggestion review) wired through client/routes.ts with navigation entries and en-US/zh-CN locale strings. Verified with unit tests, a rebuild, a live HTTP smoke test of every read and write endpoint, the Swagger document (16 /crm/ paths), and a scripted real-browser pass as both root and a sales representative (0 console or page errors; create customer/contact/opportunity/follow-up, inline status change, CSV import preview and commit, suggestion generate/approve all succeeded; the representative saw only their own records and no Settings entry, while root and the supervisor saw the whole team).

issues.title: Opportunity amount rendered as '—' in the list and customer detail
issues.symptom: Every row of the Opportunities list and the customer-detail opportunity table showed '—' for Amount, even though the API returned values (e.g. '350000') and the edit dialog prefilled the same number correctly.
issues.rootCause: crmOpportunities.amount is a decimal column. The @nocobase/db row decoder returns decimal fields as strings to preserve precision, so GET /api/crm/opportunities returned amount as '350000'. Every other CRM endpoint spread the raw row (...row), and the client formatAmount(amount: number) guards with Number.isFinite(amount), which is false for a string, so it fell through to '—'. The same leak made the assistant's high-value suggestion text read 'Worth —'.
issues.resolution: Added an opportunityView(row, owners, customerName) helper in server/crm/service.ts that coerces amount through the existing numberOrZero helper and adds ownerName/customerName, matching the declared contract (OpportunityView.amount: number, schemas.ts z.number()). Used it at all four opportunity-returning sites (customerDetail, listOpportunities, createOpportunity, updateOpportunity) and coerced the rows fed to buildSuggestionDrafts. Added an integration test in tests/logic/app-server.test.ts that signs in to an installed standalone server and asserts every returned amount is a finite number; it fails against the previous code.

issues.title: Imported customers did not appear until a manual reload
issues.symptom: After committing a CSV import, the newly created customer (Nimbus Robotics) was missing from the customers list; it appeared only after a full page reload.
issues.rootCause: client/routes.ts nests the import page (and the customer detail) under the /crm/customers route, which renders CustomersPage with an <Outlet />. The list therefore stays mounted while the import page is shown. useLoad keys its cache on `${search}|${level}|${page}`, none of which change on returning from a child route, so the effect did not refetch and the stale list was reused.
issues.resolution: Included useLocation().key in the useLoad key of client/pages/crm/customers/index.tsx. location.key changes on every navigation, so returning to the list from the import (or a detail) route refetches it; dialogs that stay on the same location still use the explicit reload(). Added tests/components/crm-customers-list.test.tsx, which navigates into the import child route and back and asserts the list reloads; it fails against the previous key.

findings.title: 权限集合/种子示例以 .js 相对导入 .ts 源，照做会在种子加载时解析失败
findings.detail: code-and-seeds.md 两处示例从 .ts 种子相对导入 .js：../../server/sales-resources.js（第 40 行）与 ../../seed-data/permission-sets.js（第 69 行）；同页第 97 行文字却说该种子导入 database/seed-data/permission-sets.ts，文档自相矛盾。@nocobase/db 的种子加载器把 .ts 源以 file URL 交给原生 import，__rewriteRelativeImportExtension 只重写 ^\.\.?/ 的字面量、不匹配 file:// URL，因此 .js 说明符解析不到实际 .ts 文件。
findings.claimed: code-and-seeds.md:40,69 的示例用 .js 相对说明符从 .ts 种子导入同仓库 .ts 模块。
findings.observed: task-loader.js:5-6 的重写仅对 ^\.\.?/ 生效，:60 传入的是 pathToFileURL().href；.ts 源按 .js 说明符解析失败。
findings.impact: 按示例写种子会加载失败；应用需把说明符改为 .ts（本次 repair-2 即如此）。
findings.suggestedChange: 把示例说明符改为 .ts（与第 97 行一致），并让 importTaskDefinition 对 .ts 源回退 .js 到 .ts。

diagnosis.trigger: 在 database/main/seeds/*.ts 中按 code-and-seeds.md 示例 import '../../seed-data/permission-sets.js' 并运行 pnpm nocobase db apply
diagnosis.expected: 示例可直接运行：.ts 种子文件的相对导入按示例解析到同仓库 .ts 模块
diagnosis.actual: 种子加载器把 file URL 交给原生 import，.js 说明符匹配不到 .ts 文件；repair-2 改成 .ts 后才通过
diagnosis.workaround: 应用把相对导入改为 .ts 说明符
diagnosis.acceptance: 在 .ts 种子中按更新后的示例导入并成功执行 pnpm nocobase db apply；或加载器对 .ts 源自动把 .js 说明符解析到 .ts

feedbackReview.reason: Skill 示例与实现/应用行为一致地被证实矛盾：code-and-seeds.md 第 40、69 行的 .ts seed 示例用 .js 相对说明符，而第 97 行文字却称导入 .ts（E29/E30/E40）；加载器对 .ts 源按原生 import 执行、不把 .js 说明符映射到 .ts（E2/E3），retro 记录应用照示例写 .js 后 28 个测试失败、改成 .ts 才通过（E136/E42）。这是可据源码与过程记录证实的 guidance-gap，非环境偶发。

checks.reason: 作为公开指引，code-and-seeds.md 给出可运行的 .ts seed 示例：第 40 行 import '../../server/sales-resources.js'、第 69 行 import '../../seed-data/permission-sets.js'（E29,E30），但同页第 97 行又称该 seed 导入 database/seed-data/permission-sets.ts，自相矛盾（E40）。Skill 承诺示例可直接用于 App seed。

task-loader 把 seed 以 pathToFileURL(...).href 交给原生 import，__rewriteRelativeImportExtension 只对 ^\.\.?/ 字面量重写且不作用于 file URL；DEFAULT_TASK_EXTENSIONS 含 .ts（E2,E3）。retro 明确 Node 原生 ESM 不做 .js→.ts 重写，.js 说明符无法解析 .ts 源（E136）。

Each context carries its own tools, and which one to use is not a free choice — see [Repository and Query](#4-repository-and-query). In short: a migration works through `builder` and `query`, and a seed writes through `repository`.

The rules are absolute, because these files are history that has already run on other machines:

- **Self-contained.** Spell out every table, field, index, constraint and metadata operation in the file. Never import a Collection definition, model, registry or shared constant that keeps evolving — that silently changes both the behavior and the checksum of something already applied.
- **Immutable once merged.** Check with `git log -- <file>` if unsure. Before the branch is merged you may correct the file in place; after it, every change is a new, later file. Never hard-code a previous checksum to make an edited migration look untouched. Correcting it in place changes nothing on its own — it is recorded as executed, so a plain apply skips it and the database keeps the schema the old file produced. `pnpm nocobase db redo` rolls the latest batch back and applies it again.
- **The file name body matches `name`**, and the name is unique across every source in the application.
- **Declare `irreversible: true`** when there is no real reverse operation, instead of writing a `down()` that quietly does nothing.
- **A seed is idempotent**, keyed on a stable business value backed by a unique constraint, so a repeated run is a no-op — `upsertOne` is the direct way to express that. A seed context has no `builder` at all, and a seed has no rollback or truncate behavior.

A backfill belongs in the migration that makes it necessary, using `query` from the same context — not in a seed.

Both run inside a transaction by default. `transaction: false` opts out, and a failure then leaves partial work behind with no history record, so take it only when the operation genuinely cannot run in one.

# Migrations and seeds

This page is the application side: where the directories live, how `pnpm nocobase db apply` runs them, how additional connections configure their tasks, and what to do about checksum drift and compiled manifests.

How to write the files themselves — the migration and seed shape, the immutability and self-containment rules, the Collection Builder, and which of `builder`, `query` and `repository` a task context should reach for — belongs to the package that owns them. Read `.agents/skills/nocobase-db/SKILL.md` sections 2 and 3 before writing one, and run `pnpm nocobase skills sync` if that file is missing.

Migrations under `database/main/migrations/` are the application's schema history. Seeds under `database/main/seeds/` insert records the application requires to run. Migrations create structure. Seeds never do.

`database/tsconfig.json` extends the server configuration so editor tooling and ESLint recognize migrations and seeds as Node source. Keep it in place when adding connection directories.

## Running

```bash
pnpm nocobase db apply
```

This applies pending migrations and then pending seeds for `database.default`, including registered plugins, ordered by name across all sources. Both halves run only what is pending, so on an already-migrated database it applies seeds alone. The template defaults to `main`. Plugin migrations, seeds and runtime default reads/writes always use this same connection; changing `database.default` changes the application system database.

Seeds are the second half of that run, so the structure a seed writes into must already exist from an earlier migration. Keep seed data fixed and reproducible — no current timestamps or random values in identifying fields — and never let a repeat run silently overwrite data a user has edited.

Use the installed version's public exports, without importing plugin internals. The application owns business logic, schedule declarations, Providers, permissions, and deployment timing. Scheduler owns scheduling projections, trigger history, and execution state. The plugin's `skills/` directory is the source of truth; do not edit the synchronized application copy under `.agents/skills/`.

## Decide Whether to Use Scheduler

The primary reason to define tasks through Scheduler is **UI observability for business administrators**. Developers define schedules and execution logic in code. Business administrators use the application's task list and detail pages to view schedules, track individual executions, and enable or disable tasks when authorized.

Tasks that do not need to be viewed and tracked through the UI must not be managed by the Scheduler plugin. Give recurring ones a `ScheduleExecutor` of their own from the application's jobs service (`jobExecutorServiceToken` in `@nocobase/app-server/jobs`), and one-off background work a `JobExecutor`; the application development Skill describes both. For administrator-visible tasks, deliver Client registration, access permissions, meaningful task names, and accurate final execution status together; successful server-side dispatch alone is incomplete.

## Then Choose the Execution Model

After deciding to use Scheduler, choose according to business complexity:

| Scenario                                                                                  | Choice          | Implementation boundary                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Periodic cleanup, cache refresh, a single report, or one business Service call            | Own target type | Short operations may complete directly; hand lengthy work to a `JobExecutor`                               |
| Staged processing, branches, persisted node state, or node-level diagnostics              | `workflow`      | Scheduler determines when to trigger; Workflow orchestrates the process and nodes call typed business code |
| A simple operation that happens hourly                                                    | Own target type | Cron alone is not a reason to introduce Workflow                                                           |
| Immediate asynchronous execution                                                          | `JobExecutor`   | No Cron Schedule is needed                                                                                 |
| A one-time delay, such as ten minutes after a request                                     | Queue `delay`   | No Cron Schedule is needed; `JobExecutor` has no delay                                                     |
| Another execution system with its own references, status queries, and completion protocol | Own target type | The same `registerTarget()` call, with `inspect()` and completion reporting for work that finishes later   |

Every schedule points at a registered target; `registerTarget()` is the target extension surface, and there is no built-in target type. `workflow` means `target.type: 'workflow'`, registered by the Workflow plugin, not an additional job wrapping a workflow. An application's own targets do not depend on the Workflow plugin. Neither approach guarantees exactly-once external business effects; design business idempotency for both.

This Skill covers the application-owned half of `@nocobase/app-plugin-ai-employee`: what the App writes, where it writes it, and what the plugin already does so the App does not rebuild it. 1. **Configure the LLM service and models** using [Configure LLM services](references/llm-configuration.md): follow its safe configuration update, startup, and single-model test rules.
2. **Write the tool first, then the skill that names it.** A tool is registered in code; a Skill references it by name and cannot define one. `ai/skills/` holds Skills only.
3. **Aggregate and register.** Static-import employees and tools in `server/ai/index.ts` through a subclass of `AIResourceRegistrar`, then call `registerAIResources()` from an App `ServiceProvider.boot()` with `aiManagerToken`. See [server-runs.md § Register App resources](references/server-runs.md#register-app-resources).
4. **Define the employee.** `defineAIEmployee()` with a stable `username`, a `systemPrompt`, an `avatar` copied from the plugin's list, and the `skills` that bring its tools — list a tool in `tools` only when no Skill names it. See [capabilities.md § Employees](references/capabilities.md#employees).
5. **Mount a chat surface** behind the readiness gate, passing `defaultEmployee` so the page opens on the App's employee rather than whichever one sorts first — the built-in `atlas` has `sort: 0` and wins by default. Set `enableAttachments` on every chat surface unless the user has said they do not want file uploads: it defaults to `false`, and a chat that cannot take a screenshot or a document is the exception. Set `enableWebSearch` as well unless the user does not want web search: it also defaults to `false`, and its toggle is usable only on a model that searches; see [chat-surfaces.md § Web search toggle](references/chat-surfaces.md#web-search-toggle). Start from the plugin's working page for the surface, task, page context or tool renderer you are building — see [source-map.md § Working examples](references/source-map.md#working-examples) for where they are and what not to copy.
6. **Verify by observation**, not by reading the source back. Run the checks below.

## Safety

- Keep secrets out of the repository and conversation; never put them in the browser-visible `client:` block. Follow [LLM configuration safety](references/llm-configuration.md#safety) for key handling and silent model-list updates.

What the interface should look like is in [`ui-guidelines.md`](ui-guidelines.md); how to write the code is in [`frontend-dev.md`](frontend-dev.md). Paths in this document are relative to its own directory: [`ui-guidelines.md`](ui-guidelines.md) and [`frontend-dev.md`](frontend-dev.md) sit beside it, the topic references are under `references/`, the record templates and reviewer prompts are under `templates/`, and the screenshot tool is under `scripts/`.

Decide before you start, and say in one sentence in your reply which workflow you are following and why.

| Workflow      | When it applies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Full workflow | Any one of: a new page that loads data or has forms or overlays; a new complete interaction (a create/edit flow, a detail drawer, a multi-step operation); a change to the page structure or main interactions; one change that touches the layout or interactions of several pages; the user asks to see the design first |
| Theme change  | The change is to theme tokens or presets: the primary color, fonts, density, radius or shadows of the whole application, or adding, changing or removing a preset. Follow ["Theme change"](#theme-change) below. No design file unless the user asks                                                                       |

      "symptom": "Every row of the Opportunities list and the customer-detail opportunity table showed '—' for Amount, even though the API returned values (e.g. '350000') and the edit dialog prefilled the same number correctly.",
      "rootCause": "crmOpportunities.amount is a decimal column. The @nocobase/db row decoder returns decimal fields as strings to preserve precision, so GET /api/crm/opportunities returned amount as '350000'. Used it at all four opportunity-returning sites (customerDetail, listOpportunities, createOpportunity, updateOpportunity) and coerced the rows fed to buildSuggestionDrafts.       "status": "resolved"

      "symptom": "POST /api/crm/suggestions/:id/decide with {decision:\"approve\"} answered 403 with reason READ_FORBIDDEN (\"Reading from this Repository is forbidden by Policy.\", domain app).       "rootCause": "The followUpWrite database permission in server/crm/resources.ts declared .create(\"*\").update(\"*\") but no .read(\"*\"). The authorization plugin folds a composite action's grants into a RepositoryPolicy in which an undeclared operation is false, and Repository.createOne/updateOne perform an internal read context before writing. Binding the edit policy therefore made every write through it fail on the read node. The other write permissions (customers, contacts, opportunities) already declared .read(\"*\"), which is why only follow-ups failed.",
      "resolution": "Added .read(\"*\") to followUpWrite so the edit action covers the read-back, consistent with the other write permissions.
